title: Native Execution Engine architecture: Gluten, Velox, and where they sit
purpose: Native Execution Engine architecture. Catalyst physical plan; Gluten plan translation; Velox vectorized execution; JVM Tungsten fallback path; Columnar to row conversion boundary.
accessibleSummary: Native Execution Engine architecture. Catalyst physical plan; Gluten plan translation; Velox vectorized execution; JVM Tungsten fallback path; Columnar to row conversion boundary.
longDescription: Native Execution Engine architecture. Catalyst physical plan; Gluten plan translation; Velox vectorized execution; JVM Tungsten fallback path; Columnar to row conversion boundary.

nodes.label: Catalyst produces the physical plan
nodes.summary: Catalyst's optimizer behaviour is fully preserved under native execution.
nodes.detail: Catalyst's optimizer behaviour is fully preserved under native execution.
nodes.whyItMatters: Catalyst's optimizer behaviour is fully preserved under native execution.

evidence.note: NEE preserves adaptive query execution, cost-based rewrites, column pruning and predicate pushdown.

processing: Optimize and produce a physical plan
drill.example: A filtered join is planned identically whether or not native execution is enabled.
failureModes: Expecting the native engine to fix a bad plan — it changes execution, not planning.

nodes.label: spark.native.enabled selects the path
nodes.summary: spark.native.enabled selects the native path per application on both runtimes.
nodes.detail: spark.native.enabled selects the native path per application on both runtimes.
nodes.whyItMatters: spark.native.enabled selects the native path per application on both runtimes.

evidence.note: Native execution is toggled per application with spark.native.enabled.
NEE supports Parquet and Delta on Runtime 1.3 and Runtime 2.0.

outputs: Native execution attempted for supported operators
drill.example: The Environment's Acceleration tab enables it for every notebook attached to that Environment.
failureModes: Enabling the toggle without verifying the plan can leave a job running entirely on the JVM.

nodes.label: Gluten translates the plan
nodes.summary: Gluten converts supported parts of the physical plan into a Substrait plan.
nodes.detail: Gluten converts supported parts of the physical plan into a Substrait plan.
nodes.whyItMatters: Gluten converts supported parts of the physical plan into a Substrait plan.

evidence.note: Gluten intercepts the optimized physical plan and converts supported portions into a Substrait plan.

drill.example: A scan, filter and hash aggregate translate while an unsupported window function does not.
controls: Gluten's operator support surface, which changes per release
failureModes: An unsupported expression inside an operator prevents that whole operator from translating.

nodes.label: Velox executes it vectorized
nodes.summary: Velox executes the translated plan as vectorized columnar C++ operators.
nodes.detail: Velox executes the translated plan as vectorized columnar C++ operators.
nodes.whyItMatters: Velox executes the translated plan as vectorized columnar C++ operators.

evidence.note: Velox is a C++ database acceleration library from Meta that performs vectorized execution.
Velox executes the Substrait plan as vectorized SIMD columnar operations.

processing: Execute vectorized C++ kernels over column batches
drill.example: A sum over one column runs as a single vectorized pass over a contiguous array rather than per-row calls.
controls: Batch size and native memory settings
failureModes: Velox semantics can diverge from JVM Spark in specific casts and rounding behaviour.

nodes.label: Measured gain, workload dependent
nodes.summary: Microsoft's TPC-DS benchmark reports up to six times open-source Spark performance.
nodes.detail: Microsoft's TPC-DS benchmark reports up to six times open-source Spark performance.
nodes.whyItMatters: Microsoft's TPC-DS benchmark reports up to six times open-source Spark performance.

evidence.note: TPC-DS at scale factor 1000 using Delta showed up to six times faster performance than open-source Spark, about 83% compute-cost savings on a fixed-size cluster.

drill.example: A scan-and-aggregate gold build completes substantially faster with no code change.
failureModes: I/O-bound work sees far less benefit than the headline benchmark suggests.

nodes.label: JVM / Tungsten executes the rest
nodes.summary: Unsupported operators fall back to standard JVM Spark automatically.
nodes.detail: Unsupported operators fall back to standard JVM Spark automatically.
nodes.whyItMatters: Unsupported operators fall back to standard JVM Spark automatically.

evidence.note: When NEE meets an unsupported operator, expression, data type or feature, that segment falls back to standard JVM Spark automatically.

outputs: Correct results via the traditional path
drill.example: A JSON source read stays on the JVM while the downstream aggregation runs natively.
controls: Query rewriting to avoid unsupported constructs
failureModes: Fallback is silent, so a performance regression can have no visible error.

nodes.label: Every boundary costs a conversion
nodes.summary: Each native-to-JVM crossing inserts a columnar-to-row conversion cost.
nodes.detail: Each native-to-JVM crossing inserts a columnar-to-row conversion cost.
nodes.whyItMatters: Each native-to-JVM crossing inserts a columnar-to-row conversion cost.

evidence.note: Gluten inserts a columnar-to-row conversion at every native/JVM boundary, so a plan falling back mid-flight can be slower than running with NEE off.

inputs: A plan alternating native and JVM operators
processing: Convert columnar batches to rows and back
drill.example: VeloxColumnarToRowExec appearing repeatedly in a plan signals repeated conversion cost.
controls: Restructure so unsupported operators sit at the plan edge, not the middle
failureModes: Many small native islands cost more in conversion than they save in execution.

nodes.label: So verification is not optional
nodes.summary: Plan suffixes, the Spark Advisor and the Diagnostics pane confirm what really ran natively.
nodes.detail: Plan suffixes, the Spark Advisor and the Diagnostics pane confirm what really ran natively.
nodes.whyItMatters: Plan suffixes, the Spark Advisor and the Diagnostics pane confirm what really ran natively.

evidence.note: Native execution can be confirmed in the Spark UI or df.explain() output via suffixes such as *Transformer.
The Fabric Spark Advisor surfaces real-time alerts when execution falls back to JVM-based Spark.

drill.example: No *Transformer suffixes anywhere with the engine enabled means the query ran entirely on the JVM.
failureModes: Trusting the configuration toggle instead of the plan hides a fully fallen-back job.

edges.label: Optimized physical plan handed to Gluten
Supported operators become a Substrait plan
Vectorized execution delivers the measured speedup
Unsupported operators stay on the JVM
